One Big Headline
CRISPR Takes on Cholesterol
An experimental gene-editing treatment lowered "bad" cholesterol and triglycerides in patients for at least a year after a single dose, according to
new results released
yesterday from an early-stage trial. Among those receiving the highest dose, bad cholesterol fell by an average of 53% and triglycerides by 48%.
The treatment uses CRISPR—a technology that allows scientists to make targeted changes to DNA—to switch off a gene in liver cells that helps regulate blood fats. Initial results released last November showed the approach worked for at least two months; the latest follow-up suggests the effect may be longer lasting. The trial involved 15 patients with severe cholesterol or triglyceride disorders. Researchers reported no serious treatment-related side effects, though larger trials are needed to assess long-term safety and effectiveness.
Watch how CRISPR works
.
Cholesterol is a waxy substance that comes in two forms, low- and high-density lipoproteins (
LDL and HDL
), while triglycerides are energy stored as fat in the bloodstream. Too much LDL, or "bad" cholesterol, can contribute to plaque buildup in blood vessels, increasing the risk of heart attack and stroke.

Quick Hits
Nepal flood death toll nears 600 as rescue efforts continue.
More than 3,700 people have been rescued as crews search for survivors following Wednesday's massive flood along the Nepal-China border. At least 579 people have been killed in Nepal and five in Tibet, while roughly 2,500 remain missing; authorities are monitoring
newly formed lakes
upstream for risks of further flooding. (

Iran war reaches six-month mark.
Six months after fighting began between Iran, Israel, and the US, diplomatic efforts have yet to produce an agreement to end the conflict. At least 18 US service members have been killed and more than 750 wounded, while the Pentagon estimates the war has cost the US more than $37.5B. (

Norway's King Harald V dies at 89 after 35 years on the throne.
Harald died yesterday after being hospitalized with a rare blood disorder and later developing a bacterial bloodstream infection. The monarch, who took the throne in 1991, is succeeded by his 53-year-old son, Haakon; Haakon's 22-year-old daughter, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, is now heir to the throne. (

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signals interest rate hikes may be needed.
Warsh yesterday said the Federal Reserve has "work to do" if underlying inflation does not move toward the central bank's 2% target quickly enough. The comments, delivered during his first Jackson Hole speech as Fed chair, led investors to increase their expectations for a September rate hike. (

Dolly Parton's music streams surge more than 2,000% after her death.
US audio and video streams of Parton's catalog jumped from 1.2 million Monday to 30.5 million Tuesday, the day the country music icon died at age 80. "Jolene" led the surge, climbing from roughly 196,000 streams to 3.3 million, while "9 to 5" jumped to 3 million. "Islands in the Stream" and "I Will Always Love You" each topped 2 million. (

Thousands rally for voting rights in Washington, DC.
Demonstrators gathered on the National Mall yesterday for the Defend the Vote march, held 63 years after Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech at the 1963 March on Washington. The rally comes amid changes to voting rules and
congressional maps
ahead of November's midterm elections. (

Humankind(ness)
Today, we're sharing a story from reader
Susan W.
in
Richmond, VA.
"I do improv outside of work. I was in a special show themed around professional wrestling. While my coworkers are supportive, they all have lives, etc. At the show, I was flabbergasted to see nine people from my work there with signs cheering me on. It was so uplifting, and I am incredibly grateful."
